The claim states that "Section 2(b)(1)(A)(ii) applies to Charlie as the dependent in 2017."

**Analysis of Statutes:**
1.  **§2(b)(1)(A)** defines the conditions for an individual to be considered a "head of household". It lists two categories of people who can support this status:
    *   (i) A **qualifying child** (as defined in section 152(c)).
    *   (ii) **Any other person** who is a dependent of the taxpayer, if the taxpayer is entitled to a deduction for such person under section 151.
    *   The phrase "any *other* person" in subsection (ii) implies that this category is for dependents who do *not* fall under subsection (i) (i.e., not qualifying children).

2.  **§152(c)** defines "Qualifying Child".
    *   (2) **Relationship**: Includes a "brother, sister, stepbrother, or stepsister of the taxpayer".
    *   (3) **Age**: Must be younger than the taxpayer and less than 25 years old at the end of the taxable year.
    *   (1)(B) **Residency**: Must have the same principal place of abode as the taxpayer for more than one-half of the taxable year.

3.  **Case Facts**:
    *   Charlie is Bob's brother.
    *   Charlie was born in 2000. In 2017, Charlie is 17 years old (less than 25).
    *   Bob furnished costs of the home where he and Charlie lived (Residency met).
    *   Bob is older than Charlie (married 1992, Charlie born 2000).
    *   Bob is entitled to a deduction for Charlie under §151(c) in 2017.

**Evaluation:**
*   Charlie meets the definition of a **Qualifying Child** under §152(c) (Relationship: Brother; Age: 17; Residency: Yes).
*   Therefore, under §2(b)(1)(A), Charlie falls under subsection **(i)** ("a qualifying child").
*   Subsection **(ii)** applies to "any *other* person" (i.e., a dependent who is *not* a qualifying child).
*   Since Charlie is a qualifying child, he does not fall under the "any other person" category of §2(b)(1)(A)(ii).
*   The claim asserts that §2(b)(1)(A)(ii) applies to Charlie. This contradicts the statutory classification that Charlie falls under §2(b)(1)(A)(i).

**Conclusion:**
The claim is incorrect because Charlie qualifies as a "qualifying child" under the provided statutes, making §2(b)(1)(A)(i) the applicable provision, not §2(b)(1)(A)(ii).
